tooltip.simpleradio_repeaters.bank: Plug into the top of a Relay attached to an antenna to allow inserted channels to be repeated.
tooltip.simpleradio_repeaters.card: Tune in a radiosmithing station, then right-click a Repeater Bank to insert.
tooltip.simpleradio_repeaters.transponde: Plug into a Relay. Left card to right cards; click the display to toggle simplex/duplex.
tooltip.simpleradio_repeaters.amplifier: Boosts Relay antenna power by 75% and resets relay decay. Inherited interference remains.
tooltip.simpleradio_repeaters.copper_amp: Boosts Relay antenna power by 25%. Does not reset relay decay.
tooltip.simpleradio_repeaters.redstone_a: Boosts Relay antenna power by 50%. Does not reset relay decay.
tooltip.simpleradio_repeaters.handbook: Right-click to read. Installed addons unlock extra chapters.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.intro:
Build a relay, tune its cards, and carry voice across linked towers.

Use the arrows to read, or jump to a topic. Extra chapters appear when their addons are installed.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.start.bod:
Build a Simple Radio antenna core with at least one antenna above it.

Attach a Relay to the core's side. Plug a Repeater Bank directly on top of the Relay.

Tune a Frequency Card at a radiosmithing station and insert it in the Bank. Match your radio's frequency AND AM/FM mode.

Insert a catalyst in the Relay. Wait for positive ANT and READY. A bare Relay and Bank cannot work.

Build another tuned tower within reach to extend the network. Verified towers keep relaying while unloaded; they do not load their chunks.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.cards.bod:
A Bank holds six cards. Each selected channel is repeated unchanged; it does not convert one channel to another.

Click a front slot with a card to fill that slot. Click elsewhere on the front to fill the first empty slot. Empty-hand click a card to remove it.

Catalysts and upgrades go in the Relay. Empty-hand click on or near their front sockets to eject them.

Sneak + empty-hand click the Relay to turn it on or off. Hoppers cannot edit the cards.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.signals.b:
A Relay receives your voice, then broadcasts it from each reachable tower on the selected channel.

Your first hop must reach a tower. Later hops must reach the next tower. The final wireless hop must reach the listener.

A large tower can reach a handheld that is too far away to reply. Test both directions.

Relaying restores carrier strength, not clean audio: the worst interference already met stays with the message. Wired receivers can also use a nearby relay's broadcast.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.catalysts:
Every Relay needs a valid catalyst AND a working antenna, even if native radios allow catalyst-free operation.

Defaults: gilded blackstone is 90%; an amethyst block is 60%. Other registered positive-strength catalysts also work.

The catalyst sets this tower's power ceiling. Each later relay visit retains 90% of that ceiling. With blackstone: 90%, 81%, 72.9%. With amethyst: 60%, 54%, 48.6%.

These are percentages of each tower's own nominal power. Server settings can change catalyst strengths.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.amplifier:
One upgrade socket, one upgrade.

Copper: +25% antenna score.
Redstone: +50%.
Ender: +75%.

A 32-point antenna contributes 40, 48 or 56 points. The boost helps Relay transmission and reception; native base power is unchanged.

Ender also resets relay decay at that tower, restoring its first-relay catalyst ceiling for the next stretch. Earlier audio interference stays.

A focus uses this same socket, so choose between amplification and its dimensional benefit.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.transpond:
Use a Transponder INSTEAD OF a Bank on top of the Relay. It has one left card and two right slots. Insert at least one tuned card on each side.

Simplex sends left to right: A on the left, B and C on the right broadcasts A as B and C.

Duplex also sends right-side channels back to the left. Click the center display to switch modes.

It translates only. To keep A live unchanged, put A on a right-side card too. It can translate signals arriving locally or through the relay network.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.troublesh:
Check READY, positive ANT, catalyst, and the module directly above the Relay. Check frequency AND AM/FM on every card and radio.

Links alone do not guarantee a long route: later relay visits lose power. Move towers closer, improve antennas, or add an Ender Amplifier.

/radiorepeaters status shows network activity. An operator can use list, refresh or diagnose. Hold the transmitting radio for a useful diagnose report.

Craft this handbook with a book and copper wire, in any arrangement. Its optional chapters update whenever you open it.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.foci.body:
With Dimensional Foci installed, direct cross-world radio is replaced by focus-equipped Relays, regardless of Simple Radio's dimensional switch. A focus shares the amplifier socket.

Nether Focus on an Overworld Relay: a weak two-way pocket at mapped Nether X/Z, high at the roof. Nether listeners may need AM, more height, or a local tower to reply.

Nether Focus on a Nether Relay: improves local reach and reliability while Nether tweaks are enabled. It does not project into the Overworld.

End Focus: projects between Overworld and End at matching X/Z. The End pocket starts at the bottom of the dimension. There is no fixed 500-block cap.

Projected pockets do not link directly to each other. Build a real relay in their target dimension to form a hub.

Nether tweaks are on by default: local distance counts x4 with extra noise; a focused Nether Relay uses x2 with lower noise. Crossings remain harsh.

An operator can restore native local Nether propagation with:
/radiofoci config netherTweaks false

Focus bridges remain enabled.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.extenders:
Directional Antenna adds the Parabolic Receiver and Wide-Angle Receiver Array. Both improve reception on their attached tower, including a native Receiver. They do not increase outgoing power.

Attach one to a vertical mast with antenna above it. Keep its 3x3 area clear. Empty-hand click turns its head 15 degrees; sneak-click turns it back. Aim stops at 45 degrees either way.

Angles below are measured to either side of the aimed direction. Both use the same maximum extra-bonus scale.

Parabolic: 100% through 30 degrees, 50% at 45, zero at 60.

Wide-angle: 75% through 45 degrees, 50% at 60, zero at 75.

The fade is smooth. Ordinary reception remains outside the beam. Overlapping receivers use the strongest bonus; they do not add together.

The bonus scales with tower power. It helps weak handhelds reach the tower and helps towers hear distant relays. Point receivers at incoming signals. They cannot clean up noise already picked up.
